channel.title: The Grant Desk - Fellowships, Media Arts, Film & Sound, weekly digest
channel.description: Paid open calls, fellowships and residencies in AI, tech, research, and digital and mixed-media arts, sorted into the right pile. Updated as new calls land on the desk. Filtered to: Fellowships, Media Arts, Film & Sound, weekly digest. Released weekly: each Sunday's drop carries one entry per grant added in the week before it (Sunday to Saturday). A call that closes before its drop goes out is not sent; the website lists those.

item.title: IAS CEU: Global Invisible University Artist and Writer in Residence Fellowships 2027/28 (Budapest, EUR 2,000 a month) (closes 30 Nov)
item.description:
Institute for Advanced Study, Central European University (IAS CEU)
Deadline: 30 Nov 2026
Award: Net allowance of EUR 2,000 a month, plus accommodation at the Raoul Wallenberg Guesthouse and/or office space at IAS CEU as available. Travel and health insurance are not covered.

Two residential fellowships within the Global Invisible University programme: one Writer in Residence (poetry, prose, drama, screen and playwriting) and one Visual or New Media Artist in Residence (from painting and film to digital art, computer graphics and interactive art).

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Schomburg Center Scholars-in-Residence 2027-28 (NYPL, Harlem; USD 35,000 long-term or USD 3,000 a month short-term; playwrights and creative writers eligible) (closes 1 Dec)
item.description:
Schomburg Center for Research in Black Culture, The New York Public Library
Deadline: 1 Dec 2026, 23:59 EST
Award: Long-term fellowship: USD 35,000 stipend. Short-term fellowship: USD 3,000 per month for one to three months. No application fee mentioned.

Residential fellowships for work on the history, politics, literature and culture of peoples of African descent that needs the Schomburg Center's collections.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: n-Space Fellowship, Singapore Fellow (Prediction): 9-month art and technology fellowship with 3 months at Somerset House Studios, London (GBP 5,000 fee, travel and accommodation covered) (closes 7 Dec)
item.description:
Somerset House Studios with the National Arts Council Singapore; research partner UAL Creative Computing Institute; supported by the Rothschild Foundation
Deadline: 7 Dec 2026, 10:00 GMT
Award: GBP 5,000 fellowship fee, plus return flights to London, accommodation, per diems and ground transport for both London visits, and access to a GBP 30,000 R&D fund shared by the six-person cohort. No application fee mentioned.

The Singapore place in the second n-Space fellowship cohort at Somerset House Studios, run with the National Arts Council Singapore.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Humboldt Residency Programme 2027, "Oceanic Horizons: The Future of our Blue Planet" (funded six-week residency for researchers, creatives and practitioners) (closes 14 Dec)
item.description:
Alexander von Humboldt Foundation
Deadline: 14 Dec 2026
Award: Monthly allowance for the six-week residency (figure not published: researchers get standard Humboldt fellowship rates, creatives and practitioners a competitive honorarium), travel allowance to and from Germany, accommodation at Schloss Wiepersdorf and a Berlin aparthotel, and a budget for public formats. No family allowance. No application fee.

Each year the Humboldt Foundation brings twelve people from research, the arts and civil society together to work on one topic and find new ways of communicating it to audiences beyond academia. The 2027 topic is Oceanic Horizons: The Future of our Blue Planet.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: W. E. B. Du Bois Research Institute Fellows Program 2027-28 (Hutchins Center, Harvard; USD 70,000 to 75,000 for the academic year) (closes 14 Dec)
item.description:
W. E. B. Du Bois Research Institute, Hutchins Center for African and African American Research, Harvard University
Deadline: 14 Dec 2026
Award: Stipends of USD 70,000 to USD 75,000 for the ten-month academic year, adjusted for one-semester fellowships. Health insurance is not provided. No application fee.

The Fellows Program is the oldest activity of the W. E. B. Du Bois Research Institute, which has appointed fellows since 1975.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Ox-Bow Summer Fellowship 2027: twelve-week live-work fellowship in Michigan (USD 300 weekly stipend, room, board and studio) (closes 3 Jan 2027)
item.description:
Ox-Bow School of Art and Artists' Residency
Deadline: 3 Jan 2027
Award: USD 300 weekly stipend for twelve weeks, a travel stipend for arrival and departure (amount not published), a private room, all meals and a dedicated studio. In exchange fellows work 20 hours a week on campus operations. No application fee is mentioned.

Ox-Bow's Summer Fellowship is a twelve-week live-work programme on its lagoon-side campus in Saugatuck, Michigan.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Fine Arts Work Center Visual Arts Fellowship 2027-28: seven months in Provincetown (USD 1,300 monthly stipend, apartment and studio) (closes 7 Feb 2027)
item.description:
Fine Arts Work Center in Provincetown
Deadline: 7 Feb 2027
Award: USD 1,300 monthly stipend for seven months, a USD 1,000 exit stipend to support relocation, a furnished apartment and a studio of about 400 square feet. Application fee USD 40 to 65 depending on date (USD 55 until 1 December, then USD 65); limited fee waivers on request.

The Fine Arts Work Center gives emerging visual artists seven months of time, housing and a studio in Provincetown, on the tip of Cape Cod. WHO: visual artists aged 18 or over at an early stage of their careers. No MFA is required.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Los Angeles Reporting Collective: LARC 2027 Fellowship (Southern California, USD 600 stipend) (closes 23 Nov)
item.description:
Los Angeles Reporting Collective (LARC)
Deadline: 23 Nov 2026
Award: USD 600 project stipend, paid on completing the training phase, with possible extra funding for project expenses

Yearlong journalism training and mentorship programme for local reporters and nonfiction storytellers. Fellows get 12 free workshops (8 online, 4 in person in Los Angeles), a one-on-one mentor, newsroom shadowing and free conference access, then produce their own project with a USD 600 stipend.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: MPI Short Film Lab 2027: narrative short film lab with fellowship grants and a USD 10,000 script grant (theme: For the Greater Good?) (closes 29 Nov)
item.description:
Moving Picture Institute (MPI)
Deadline: 29 Nov 2026, 23:59 PST
Award: Filmmakers accepted into the lab receive fellowship grants (amount not published). One official selection receives a USD 10,000 grant, which includes MPI acquiring the script for further development. Travel support for the Los Angeles summit is not mentioned. No application fee mentioned.

The Moving Picture Institute is a production company and talent incubator that makes films about human freedom. Its Short Film Lab takes writer-directors from a concept to a finished short script, and can lead to production as an MPI Original film. THEME 2027: For the Greater Good?

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: OCA: Liu Pursuits Aperture Project Fellowships 2027 (documentary and archives, USD 10,000 stipend) (closes 29 Nov)
item.description:
OCA Asian Pacific American Advocates and the Liu Pursuits Foundation
Deadline: 29 Nov 2026
Award: USD 10,000 stipend per fellow (USD 5,000 at the halfway mark, USD 5,000 at the end), plus an equipment rental budget, and travel, lodging and food per diem on production trips

Four part-time, year-long fellowships (two Documentary Fellows, two Archives Fellows) on the Aperture Project, a documentary series telling Asian American and Pacific Islander stories through OCA chapters.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Kinship: Nature Culture Fellowship 2027 (online; micro-grants of USD 1,000 to 2,000 for selected fellows) (closes 1 Dec)
item.description:
Kinship
Deadline: 1 Dec 2026
Award: Micro-grants of USD 1,000 to 2,000 plus mentorship for selected fellows' community projects; not every fellow is funded

Global fellowship on culture, storytelling and ecological change for artists, storytellers, scientists, educators, community organisers, researchers and activists aged 18 and over.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: n-Space Fellowship, second cohort (Prediction): 18-month research fellowship at Somerset House Studios, London (GBP 10,000 fee plus shared GBP 30,000 R&D fund) (closes 7 Dec)
item.description:
Somerset House Studios, with UAL Creative Computing Institute, Abandon Normal Devices, Lancaster University and the National Arts Council Singapore; supported by the Rothschild Foundation
Deadline: 7 Dec 2026, 10:00 GMT
Award: London track: GBP 10,000 fee and access to a GBP 30,000 shared R&D fund, with 24/7 workspace. No travel, relocation or accommodation support. Singapore track: GBP 5,000 fee plus return flights, accommodation, per diems and ground transport, and the same shared fund. Up to GBP 200 towards an access support worker for the application. No application fee mentioned.

n-Space at Somerset House Studios is a space for experimental, collaborative research across art, technology and society, aimed at outcomes that do not fit traditional institutional platforms. Its second fellowship cohort is convened around PREDICTION.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Drama League: Rose Directing Fellowship 2027 (US directors; up to USD 14,250, flights and housing, three months at the Rose Theatre, London) (closes 4 Jan 2027)
item.description:
The Drama League, in partnership with Rose Theatre, Kingston upon Thames
Deadline: 4 Jan 2027
Award: USD 950 a week for up to 15 weeks (maximum USD 14,250), up to USD 200 health insurance reimbursement, round-trip economy airfare for each leg, and housing in New York (for those outside the metro area), Pittsburgh and London. No application fee mentioned.

One fellowship a year for an American director who wants to work beyond the United States. WHAT YOU DO: join the Drama League's Directors Project Week in New York (18 to 22 May 2027) and a retreat at Carnegie Mellon University in Pittsburgh (23 to 28 May), then spend 2 August to 31 October 2027 at...

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Craigardan Trillium Fellowship 2027 (residency for artists, activists and scholars of color, USD 4,600 + USD 500 honorarium) (closes 15 Dec)
item.description:
Craigardan
Deadline: 15 Dec 2026
Award: USD 4,600 fellowship toward a minimum two-week residency (covers the residency fee), plus a USD 500 honorarium. Travel, materials and personal expenses are not covered. USD 25 application fee (waivers available on request).

The Trillium Fellowship supports artists, activists and scholars of color working in any discipline who would benefit from the time and space to pursue their work or find creative retreat at Craigardan, a residency and farm in the Adirondacks.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Kala Art Institute: Media Arts Fellowship 2027-28 (Berkeley; USD 3,000 stipend) (closes 1 Mar 2027)
item.description:
Kala Art Institute
Deadline: 1 Mar 2027
Award: USD 3,000 stipend plus facility access.

Kala's long-running Media Arts Fellowship supports four artists working in film and video, sound, animation, performance cinema and media installation. ELIGIBILITY: local, national and international artists not enrolled in a degree programme.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Schloss Wiepersdorf Individual and Collaborative Fellowships 2028 (Brandenburg; EUR 1,200/month plus room and board) (closes 15 Apr 2027)
item.description:
Schloss Wiepersdorf (state of Brandenburg)
Deadline: 15 Apr 2027, 23:59 CEST
Award: EUR 1,200 per month stipend, a one-time EUR 480 material grant, room and board, and German visa costs where needed. No application fee.

Three-month residential fellowships at Schloss Wiepersdorf for artists, writers, composers and scholars from Germany and abroad. Fellows get room, board, a EUR 1,200 monthly stipend and a material grant; fine artists get a studio where space allows.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: IIE x OceanX Ocean Futures Fellowship 2027-28 (remote, monthly stipend; AI, immersive media and digital archives tracks) (closes 17 Nov)
item.description:
Institute of International Education (IIE) with OceanX
Deadline: 17 Nov 2026, 23:59 EST
Award: Monthly stipend (amount not published), plus a technology stipend for some fellows case by case. No application fee.

A 12-month remote fellowship from IIE and the ocean-exploration organisation OceanX for recent graduates using digital media, immersive storytelling and technology to connect ocean science with the public.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: CCA-WRI Research Fellowship 2027: Vacancy (Montreal; CAD 5,000/month) (closes 30 Nov)
item.description:
Canadian Centre for Architecture with the Window Research Institute
Deadline: 30 Nov 2026
Award: CAD 5,000 per month for up to 3 months, plus travel and visa support.

Four fellowships study vacancy as a cyclical condition: climate crisis, demolition and material cycles, vacancy planned through policy, and vacancy caused by pollution or extraction.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Florence Levy Kay Postdoctoral Fellowship in Computer Music and Engineering (Brandeis University) 2027-2029 (closes 15 Dec)
item.description:
Brandeis University (Department of Music and Engineering)
Deadline: 15 Dec 2026, 23:59 EST
Award: USD 64,000 for the nine-month year (lecturer rank), plus USD 4,000 a year for research and travel and negotiable first-year relocation. No application fee.

A two-year postdoctoral fellowship in computer music and engineering: human/machine music-making, signal processing, and instrument and interface design, hosted by Brandeis Music and Engineering.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Folger Institute Artistic Research Fellowships 2027-28 (USD 4,000 to 5,000 per month) (closes 15 Jan 2027)
item.description:
Folger Shakespeare Library (Folger Institute)
Deadline: 15 Jan 2027, 23:59 EST
Award: USD 4,000 per virtual month or USD 5,000 per onsite month.

Artistic research fellowships for artists whose work needs primary research on the early modern world (about 1400 to 1800) and its legacies, using the Folger's collections. ELIGIBILITY: any artist; no degree required and no citizenship rule stated.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: KB Fellowship at NIAS 2027-2028 (National Library of the Netherlands collections incl. born-digital; artists and researchers) (closes 15 Mar 2027)
item.description:
NIAS-KNAW (Netherlands Institute for Advanced Study) with the KB, National Library of the Netherlands
Deadline: 15 Mar 2027, 12:00 CET
Award: Personal stipend (figure not published); scholars at Dutch institutions get a Dutch University Grant paid to their institution instead. Office, subsidised Amsterdam housing where eligible (otherwise local transport reimbursement). No application fee.

One fellowship a year for work with the KB's collections, facilities and expertise, including its large digitised and born-digital holdings.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: ARCAthens: Athens Residency Fellowships (Spring 2027) (closes 14 Nov)
item.description:
ARCAthens
Deadline: 14 Nov 2026, 23:00 EST
Award: Fully funded: housing, travel, a Fellowship Prize and a weekly stipend (most recent published terms, Fall 2026: USD 3,000 Fellowship Prize and USD 200/week stipend, round-trip airfare reimbursed). No application fee.

The Athens Residency is the flagship program of ARCAthens, a not-for-profit founded in 2017, offering fully funded Fellowships for visual artists and curators to live and work in Athens.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Hong Kong PhD Fellowship Scheme 2027/28 (HKD 344,400 a year for up to three years; 400 fellowships, practice-led art PhDs included) (closes 1 Dec)
item.description:
Research Grants Council (RGC) of Hong Kong, with eight Hong Kong universities
Deadline: 1 Dec 2026, 12:00 Hong Kong time
Award: Annual stipend of HKD 344,400 (about USD 44,150) plus a conference and research travel allowance of HKD 14,400 a year, for up to three years (2026/27 rates as published by the RGC). Some universities add top-ups: HKBU lists a HKD 40,000-a-year Elite Scholar Award for three years, a further HKD 20,000 travel top-up, four years of tuition waiver and two years of guaranteed accommodation. 400 fellowships for 2027/28.

The Hong Kong PhD Fellowship Scheme, run by the Research Grants Council, funds around 400 new full-time PhD students a year at eight Hong Kong universities, in any discipline, including AI, computing and data science programmes and practice-led art research (Hong Kong Baptist University's Academy...

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Sundance Institute: 2027 Graton Fellowship (USD 25,000 for California Native artists) (closes 1 Dec)
item.description:
Sundance Institute, Indigenous Program
Deadline: 1 Dec 2026, 16:30 MST
Award: USD 25,000 cash grant to each of 2 fellows, plus a yearlong support programme. No application fee.

The Graton Fellowship, run by the Sundance Institute Indigenous Program, supports two Native storytellers from California tribes with an unrestricted cash grant and a year of creative and professional support from Sundance, including mentorship and access to Institute programmes.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Museum of Fine Arts, Houston: Core Residency Program 2027-29 (USD 100,000 over 23 months, artists and critical writers) (closes 8 Jan 2027)
item.description:
Core Residency Program, Glassell School of Art, Museum of Fine Arts, Houston (MFAH)
Deadline: 8 Jan 2027
Award: USD 100,000 (USD 50,000 per year) plus a health and wellness stipend, private studio, and free or discounted Glassell School classes. Application fee USD 12.

Two-year residency for exceptional, highly motivated emerging artists and critical writers committed to developing a sustainable practice.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: School for Advanced Research: Native Artist Fellowships 2027 (USD 15,000 plus Santa Fe residency) (closes 15 Jan 2027)
item.description:
School for Advanced Research, Indian Arts Research Center
Deadline: 15 Jan 2027
Award: USD 15,000 stipend plus housing, studio space, a supplies allowance and travel. No application fee stated.

The Indian Arts Research Center at the School for Advanced Research offers three residential fellowships for Native American artists: the Eric and Barbara Dobkin Fellowship for Native women artists working in any media (including digital art and film/video), the Ronald and Susan Dubin Fellowship...

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Vision Maker Media: Creative Shorts Fellowship (up to USD 25,000 for emerging Native filmmakers, rolling)
item.description:
Vision Maker Media
Deadline: Rolling, apply any time
Award: Up to USD 25,000 production funding, plus USD 5,000 paid separately to the mentor. No application fee shown.

Vision Maker Media's Creative Shorts Fellowship funds emerging Native filmmakers to make a short film of 40 minutes or less (documentary, drama, experimental or animation), with guidelines inviting work that pushes the limits of art and technology.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Oregon Media Arts Fellowship 2026 (two USD 5,000 awards for Oregon media artists)
item.description: Portland Art Museum (PAM CUT) and Oregon Arts Commission · deadline 15 Nov 2026 · Two fellowships of USD 5,000 each, no matching funds required; paid within two months of notification. No application fee.
